## Week 5 (Oct 8) {#week-5-oct-8}

We completed the Gregory lab and began discussing deep-ocean heat uptake and fast and slow climate responses.

- **Gregory plots from CMIP6:** diagnose radiative forcing and feedback from a climate-model experiment. <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/gregory_cmip6.ipynb" download>Download notebook</a>

**[Download the Gregory lab and supporting files](week05_labs.zip)** and unzip them before opening the notebook. The package includes saved CMIP6 annual means: set `USE_SAVED_MEANS = True` to use these instead of reading cloud data. Keep the `data` folder beside the notebook.

[Slides (PDF)](../slides/week05.pdf) · [Running instructions](week05_README.txt) · [Python packages](week05_requirements.txt)

## Week 6 (Oct 15) {#week-6-oct-15}

After discussing surface–deep-ocean heat uptake and two time scales, we will work with a one-dimensional energy balance model across latitude.

- **[Regional climate: a 1D energy balance model](latitude_ebm.ipynb)**: begin with an independent model at each latitude, compare with Earth's temperature and radiation patterns, then add horizontal heat transport. <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/latitude_ebm.ipynb" download>Download notebook</a>

All model code is supplied. Answer one short question after each section; Section 5 (diffusion alone) is optional.

**[Download the notebook and its data](week06_labs.zip)** and unzip them before opening the notebook. Keep the `data` folder beside it. The package includes the NCEP temperature file, so the lab can run offline; a missing file will be downloaded from NOAA when the notebook runs.

[Week 6 slides (PDF)](../slides/week06.pdf) · [Running instructions](week06_README.txt) · [Python packages](week06_requirements.txt)

## Weeks 10–11 (Nov 12 and 19) {#week-10-nov-12}

### 1. Fitting the Keeling curve {#keeling-curve-ml}

Learn a function from the Mauna Loa CO₂ record, then compare its predictions with later observations. We fit a line, a quadratic, a model with an annual cycle, and a neural network. All code is supplied; pause at the prediction and discussion prompts. The final section compares testing on a middle block of years with testing beyond the training period.

- <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/keeling_curve_ml.ipynb" download="keeling_curve_ml.ipynb">Download the notebook</a> · [Read the notebook with plots](keeling_curve_ml.html)

Open the notebook in the course [LEAP Jupyter environment](https://leap.2i2c.cloud/) and run the cells in order. The data-reading cell downloads fixed classroom data from our course GitHub repository. **No separate data-folder download is needed.** The first run needs internet access; saved files can be reused offline.

### 2. Emissions-driven models of atmospheric CO₂ {#keeling-curve-dynamics}

Keep quadratic-plus-sine as a reference, introduce a one-box carbon budget through the EBM analogy, and compare it with a richer carbon response. Change future emissions while retaining the fitted parameters. This notebook runs independently of Notebook 1; detailed calibration is outside the main teaching sequence.

- <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/keeling_curve_dynamics.ipynb" download="keeling_curve_dynamics.ipynb">Download the notebook</a> · [Read the notebook with plots](keeling_curve_dynamics.html)

The first cell retrieves the fixed data and numerical helper from the course GitHub repository. **Download just the notebook** and run it in LEAP; no separate data folder or helper download is needed. Historical emissions end in 2024, so this notebook compares all models over 2017–2024. Notebook 1 also includes 2025 concentration observations.

[Optional offline package: both notebooks, data, and helper](keeling_curve_notebooks.zip). Individual offline packages: [regression](keeling_curve_ml.zip) · [dynamical models](keeling_curve_dynamics.zip). These student packages contain no instructor answers.

### Generating synthetic weather {#generating-synthetic-weather}

Learn a seasonal temperature distribution and day-to-day persistence from the NYC observations used in Lab 0c. Generate independent and persistent weather sequences with the same seasonal mean and spread, then compare histograms, anomaly correlations, hot-day counts, and hot-spell lengths with held-out observations. The notebook connects memory to EBM relaxation and closes with the connection to modern generative AI.

- <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/generative_weather.ipynb" download="generative_weather.ipynb">Download the notebook</a> · [Read the notebook with plots](generative_weather.html)

Open the notebook in the course [LEAP Jupyter environment](https://leap.2i2c.cloud/). The data-reading cell retrieves a fixed version from the course GitHub and caches it locally. **Download just the notebook**; no separate data folder is needed.

Allow about **30–40 minutes**; all code is supplied, with four Lab questions and an optional memory experiment. NumPy, pandas, and Matplotlib are required. No GPU is needed. The [optional offline package](generative_weather.zip) includes the notebook, reading view, and data.
